The PKGBUILD defines standard sources: a release binary ZIP from the official GitHub repository, an icon file from a pinned commit, and a local shell script. All `source` entries point to legitimate, expected locations related to the Arduino IDE project. There is no command substitution, `pkgver()` function, or top-level code execution outside of standard variable assignments. The `sha256sums` are provided and not set to 'SKIP', so the integrity of the downloaded files will be verified during extraction. The commands `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` will only source the PKGBUILD, fetch and verify the sources — none of which involve executing untrusted code or performing dangerous operations at this stage. The script is a simple wrapper to launch the Arduino IDE binary with optional user-defined flags. It sets a default `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` if not already defined, then checks for a configuration file (`arduino-flags.conf`) in the user's config directory. If present, it reads and parses the file by stripping comments and converting newlines to spaces to form a string of command-line arguments. The script uses `exec` to replace the current process with the Arduino IDE binary located at `/opt/arduino-ide/arduino-ide`, passing any command-line arguments (`$@`) and the parsed user flags. All operations are confined to user-controlled paths or fixed system locations, and there is no network access, code evaluation (e.g., `eval`, `base64`, `curl`), or file manipulation beyond reading a user configuration file — a standard and safe practice. This behavior is consistent with typical AUR packaging for binary applications and poses no evidence of malicious activity.
